sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal State; Alberta applies Common Law; Quebec applies Civil Law; federal statutes and national treaties apply throughout Canada)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, effective 2018)
CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, provisionally applied 2017)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, effective 2014)
Canada-US Income Tax Convention (1980, as amended through the 2007 Protocol)
Canada-UK Income Tax Agreement (1966, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, including the Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register provisions; Business Corporations Regulation, Alta Reg 119/2021; FINTRAC guidance and interpretation notices under the PCMLTFA.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document for each director, UBO, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Office or national identity authority of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization at a Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking relationship and source of funds for the proposed contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate registry extract for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate for UBOs and directors domiciled in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, if triggered by risk assessment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English or French translation of any non-English or non-French corporate or personal document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of translator's signature followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Sergei Magnitsky Law, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, and the FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) definitions. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, close associates, and family members; ongoing transaction monitoring and re-screening are prescribed under FINTRAC guidance. The Alberta Corporate Registry conducts a standard identity check, while the federal ISC register supports law enforcement and tax authority access. For a low-risk DTC cosmetics e-commerce entity using payment rails (Shopify Payments, PayPal), Tier-1 simplified due diligence is acceptable, but 25% UBO identification, source-of-funds verification, and records retention of at least 5 years remain mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via authorized Registry Agents using the CORES (Corporate Registry Electronic System) platform; official name search through the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) preliminary name search report.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English, French, or a combination thereof using the Latin alphabet; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for NUANS search purposes. The corporate name must be distinct from existing names and trademarks in Alberta; for a ULC, the name must include 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or the French equivalent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any word implying a connection with the Crown, a government body, or a regulated profession without prior ministerial or regulatory consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS preliminary name search report is valid for 90 days and may be extended by filing a fresh NUANS report or a new name reservation request before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of the Alberta Corporate Registry providing a new NUANS report with supporting distinctiveness arguments; if the refusal is sustained, the applicant may submit a new name reservation or appeal the Registrar's decision to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Administrative review procedures under the Alberta Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act apply to decisions of the Corporate Registry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible conditionally. The Alberta Business Corporations Act requires a registered office with a physical street address in Alberta; virtual office services that provide a physical Alberta street address, mail forwarding, and acceptance of service at that physical address are accepted. A P.O. Box alone is not permitted. For a DTC cosmetics e-commerce entity, a virtual registered office is commercially acceptable and does not trigger additional regulatory scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated under 5% annual probability for a low-risk online retail entity). Alberta corporate registries conduct primarily document-based reviews; unannounced physical inspection is unlikely unless red-flag indicators arise, such as returned corporate mail, inconsistent registered office records, or a FINTRAC money-laundering indicator triggered by the payment rails.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS preliminary name search report and corporate name reservation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized Alberta registry agent (Service Alberta statutory tariff)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (CAD 45) plus prevailing market agent fee (USD equivalent at 1.37 CAD/USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee (Articles of Incorporation for ULC)
Virtual registered office service, first year (physical Alberta street address and mail forwarding)
ISC (Individuals with Significant Control) register, corporate records book, and organizational minute book setup
Notarization and Hague Apostille or consular legalization bundle per principal (identity, address, bank reference, police clearance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Global Affairs Canada (Apostille Service), or Canadian consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; Global Affairs Canada apostille fee is CAD 30 per document (USD equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening per UBO, director, and authorized signatory (UN, OFAC, SEMA, Magnitsky, EU/UK integrated lists)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT screening data provider (e.g., World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per individual screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English/French translation of any non-English or non-French documents (if required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 7 (incorporation), 11-13 (articles), 16-17 (registered office), 101 (board of directors), and the Alberta ULC provisions applicable to unlimited liability corporations; ancillary regulations under the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry - Service Alberta (online corporate registry system and authorized NUANS search providers)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under Alberta corporate regulations) resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation; organizational board minutes retained in statutory corporate records
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no mandatory escrow account requirement under the ABCA for a standard Alberta ULC; authorized unlimited liability shares may be issued for nominal consideration, with receipt evidenced by the share subscription ledger and directors' resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers accept the allotment of one hundred (100) common voting shares in the capital of the Company, fully paid as set forth in the incorporation records. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established and maintained in the Province of Alberta at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and that corporate records be kept there. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] be appointed first directors and officers as Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, respectively, each to serve until successor appointment or removal under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). RESOLVED, that the Company adopt Bylaw No. 1 and immediately complete all statutory registrations, tax filings, and bank account opening procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NUANS Automated Name Search - Service Alberta and authorized Corporate Registry agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed ULC name and obtain the official name search report; file a Name Reservation Request where needed to hold the approved name for 90 days; incorporate using the exact approved name with the 'ULC' suffix permitted for unlimited liability corporations.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with ULC suffix
Consent to use of personal or third-party name (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused as confusing or prohibited, submit up to three alternative names per retry or request written reconsideration from the Alberta Corporate Registry within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and Alberta legal counsel acting under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation using the Alberta ULC template setting out unlimited liability share classes, class rights, initial directors, and a physical registered office address in Alberta; all incorporators execute the Articles; each named director executes a Consent to Act as Director; record subscriber signatures for share subscription.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queries arise on the draft, amend share condition clauses by supplementary articles before filing; re-execution by all incorporators is required for any substantive revision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - Online Incorporation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the registration fee and file the executed Articles electronically (or by registered mail) with the Alberta Corporate Registry; the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which evidences the commencement of the ULC's legal existence, incorporation date, and Alberta jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is requisitioned, cure the deficiency within 30 days by resubmitting corrected Articles or responding to the Deputy Registrar's notice; optional priority processing reduces turnaround to approximately one hour.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Resolutions, Bylaws, and Initial Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC; Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to adopt Bylaw No. 1, appoint officers, confirm the registered office and records address, approve the pro-forma first board resolution, issue share certificates against subscription consideration, and authorize the opening of corporate bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Share certificate ledger and subscription agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Irregularities in share issuance or officer appointment are cured by subsequent unanimous shareholder resolution or by restated articles; Alberta is a common law province, so no notarization is required for internal corporate documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Alberta Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company for a nine-digit Business Number (BN); enrol for GST/HST (mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 annually, with voluntary registration available), payroll, and import/export accounts where applicable; confirm provincial compliance by using the BN for Alberta corporate tax; file the initial annual return within 60 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Directors' and officers' legal names, addresses, dates of birth, and identification
Estimated annual revenue for GST/HST determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is delayed or mismatched, contact CRA Business Inquiries for correction; an inactive or reassigned BN can be reactivated by filing all applicable nil or corrective returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing authority in the city or town of the registered office under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26 (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence and Registration or City of Edmonton Corporate Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a general municipal business licence, or a home-based business licence if operating from a residence, before commencing commercial activity; present the Certificate of Incorporation and premises documentation; obtain building occupancy and fire safety clearance for any storage area; maintain public liability insurance.
required_dossiers: Lease, ownership document, or homeowner consent for premises
Fire safety and occupancy certificate (where storage or retail premises are used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A licence refusal or onerous condition may be appealed to the municipality's subdivision and development appeal board within 21 days of the decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial or manufacturing licence is required for online-only retail of cosmetics; premises compliance is governed by the municipal licensing authority under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26, and by Alberta Safety Codes authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (online retail and warehouse/storage use); federal Cosmetic Notification to Health Canada is a post-filing product compliance requirement, not a formation licensing precondition.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) and Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable: retail distribution and warehousing of finished cosmetic products do not trigger a Full EIA Report or Registration under Schedule 1 of the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC emissions from the retail operation; ventilation and product storage must comply with the Alberta Fire Code and Building Code; solid waste and recycling handled under applicable municipal waste-management bylaws; all cosmetics sold must satisfy the Food and Drugs Act (Canada) and Cosmetic Regulations regarding ingredient disclosure, prohibited substances (mercury, lead, restricted preservatives), traceability, and labelling safety.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and building occupancy permit required for any commercial storage or fulfillment area under the Alberta Building Code and Fire Code; a workplace hazard assessment, first-aid equipment, and worker safety training are mandated under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) with e-service portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-business-portal.html). New business registration is also available via the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal. The corporate income tax of Alberta is administered by the CRA under a federal-provincial collection agreement with Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial corporate tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the ULC under the Alberta Business Corporations Act through the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES system), obtaining the incorporation number, articles of incorporation and certificate; no minimum capital is required and non-resident ownership is permitted. Step 2: Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) by filing through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO), by telephone, or by submitting Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with certified English or French corporate documents to the CRA International and Non-Resident Taxation Services Office. Step 3: Open program accounts within the BN: RT (GST/HST), RC (corporate income tax), RP (payroll) and RM (import/export). Step 4: Register for GST/HST once the ULC is not a small supplier (taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters), or voluntarily register to recover input tax credits; a non-resident ULC must provide a Canadian address for service and may appoint an authorized GST/HST representative under Excise Tax Act section 273. Step 5: For the Alberta corporate income tax account, no separate provincial registration is required because CRA collects the Alberta tax on behalf of Alberta; the ULC must still comply with Alberta annual return filings at the Corporate Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: For Canadian domestic tax purposes, the ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation resident in Canada subject to entity-level federal Part I tax and Alberta provincial corporate income tax on worldwide income. However, due to its hybrid nature, it is eligible for pass-through treatment at the shareholder level for US federal tax purposes (disregarded entity or partnership by analogy), and Alberta partnership/ULL rules permit unlimited liability flow-through to members. For GST/HST purposes, the ULC is a separate registrant and cannot disregard the GST/HST account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (1) US federal check-the-box election on Form 8832 to treat the Canadian ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership, which is recognized for Canada-US treaty purposes with respect to US shareholders; (2) Excise Tax Act section 273 election appointing a GST/HST representative for non-resident registrants; (3) Excise Tax Act section 156 election to have supplies between a registrant and a closely related corporation deemed made for nil consideration, enabling GST/HST pooling for related Cosmetics DTC entities; (4) Quick Method of Accounting election (GST/HST) for small suppliers and the Streamlined Accounting Method for sales through a third-party fulfillment center; (5) hybrid mismatch planning where the ULC remains a corporation for CRA purposes but is flow-through for US purposes, subject to applicable CFC and subpart F rules; (6) treaty claims under the Canada-US Tax Treaty for reduced withholding and effective permanent establishment thresholds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: No separate tax-exempt zone status is available in Alberta; the ULC is subject to the normal territorial scope of Canadian taxation on worldwide income, except that foreign business income of a Canadian-resident corporation is generally taxable but foreign tax credits are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax). In Alberta, only the 5% federal GST applies; there is no provincial sales tax, no provincial component of HST, and no retail sales tax. Thus the combined headline indirect tax rate in the jurisdiction is 5.0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 taxable supplies in any single calendar quarter or over the four immediately preceding consecutive calendar quarters (the small supplier threshold). Voluntary registration is available for non-residents and e-commerce exporters to recover GST/HST input tax credits; registration is effective from the date of the application.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a mandatory real-time tax clearance, government e-invoicing authorization, API-fiscal stamping or digital clearance regime for B2B or B2C GST/HST invoices. A voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework based on the PEPPOL standard is being adopted from 2023 onwards, with participation mandatory only for certain suppliers to the federal government. Electronic GST/HST return filing (NETFILE) is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable revenues exceeding CAD 1 million; smaller registrants may file electronically voluntarily. The ULC must retain and produce, upon CRA request, a standard GST/HST invoice (BN/RT number, supplier and recipient name, transaction date, description, GST amount, and unique invoice identifier) for a minimum of six years. Payment service providers (Shopify Payments, PayPal) are not required to perform tax pre-clearance on each transaction, but CRA may issue a compliance demand for transaction-level data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The online sale of cosmetics and personal care products shipped from Alberta to a foreign customer qualifies for zero-rating under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V, section 1 (supply of tangible personal property exported by the supplier) and section 13 (delivery to a common carrier for export), provided the ULC obtains and retains documentary proof of export before filing the relevant GST/HST return or within a reasonable period thereafter. Services supplied entirely outside Canada, including digital beauty consultations and subscription content that is delivered and enjoyed offshore, are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, section 7. The goods must physically leave Canada within a reasonable time under the sale contract; supplies delivered to a Canadian freight forwarder, a Canadian fulfillment hub or a Canadian residential address do not qualify. On a zero-rated export, the ULC recovers the 5% GST embedded in its Canadian purchases through the input tax credit mechanism, resulting in a perfectly refunded export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A or ACI eManifest export reporting submitted to the Canada Border Services Agency)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / courier manifest (DHL, FedEx, UPS) evidencing the physical shipment from Canada to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the cosmetics, quantities, value, and foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, PayPal/Shopify Payments settlement report, or bank statement proving payment in foreign currency and repatriation of funds
Customer purchase order or contract containing international delivery terms (Incoterms, e.g., FOB, EXW, CIF) and destination address outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA conducts targeted audits of e-commerce exporters, including beauty DTC retailers, to verify zero-rated export claims. If the mandatory customs documentation bundle is missing, incomplete, or internally inconsistent, CRA will reassess the supply as taxable at 5% GST, disallow the related input tax credits, and charge interest compounded daily on the net tax owing. Penalty exposure includes: (a) ETA s. 280(1) penalty of CAD 100 plus 25% of the tax sought to be evaded for false statements or omissions on a return; (b) ETA s. 285(1) gross negligence penalty of 25% of the net tax understatement; (c) administrative monetary penalties under ETA s. 280.1 for failure to provide required information; and (d) criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 for knowingly evading GST/HST, with fines payable to the Crown and imprisonment of up to five years. The normal GST/HST reassessment period is four years, but where fraud, neglect, carelessness or wilful default is established, reassessment is unlimited in time. Failure to repatriate export sales proceeds within the 180-day benchmark will not automatically invalidate a zero-rating claim under ETA, but CRA will treat it as a serious indicator of unreported taxable Canadian supply and will extend the audit window and apply retrospective interest and penalties on any clawed-back refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - note: foreign exchange administration is under the Minister of Finance and the Currency Act; the Bank of Canada is the central bank. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers AML. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates banks. The Exchange Control... Actually Canada abolished foreign exchange controls in 1951 and the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed... The Foreign Exchange Control Regulations were revoked. Canada's exchange control regime is largely liberalized. The Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, the Payment Clearing and Settlement Act, and the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) govern. annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) for an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / Registrar of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the anniversary of incorporation (or amalgamation/continuation) each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a prescribed late penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to issue notice and dissolve the ULC by certificate of dissolution. Directors may also face administrative fines under ABCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and current director details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (verified on demand by the Director)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Alberta Annual Return; ISC register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance or false entry in the ISC register is an offence under ABCA, carrying potential fines, director liability, and refusal of registry services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta corporate tax allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the ULC's fiscal year; no separate Alberta corporate tax return if the T2 reports Alberta taxable income.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; a third consecutive late-filing offence triggers additional penalties under ITA section 163. Directors may be personally liable for unremitted withholdings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, every Alberta ULC must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, consent in writing to dispense with the auditor. No automatic Audit is triggered by revenue size or asset threshold under ABCA; mandatory audit applies to a reporting issuer, an entity whose articles require audit, or any ULC where the shareholders do not waive the statutory auditor requirement. CRA or the Registrar may also require audited financial statements in specified enforcement circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS (Part I) may be used, but a private Alberta ULC typically adopts Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II). IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta ULC must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC), updated within 15 days of any share transfer or change in control. At each Annual Return filing, the corporation must confirm its current registered office and director composition. The ISC register and underlying registers must be provided to the Director of Corporations or law enforcement upon demand; the Annual Return itself is a sworn/declaration-based confirmation of the corporation's record truthfulness.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–12,000 depending on transaction volume and IFRS/ASPE complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined general corporate rate (15.0% federal Part I + 8.0% Alberta provincial flat rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No cannabis-specific tax holidays; Alberta ULC not eligible for the Small Business Deduction if foreign-controlled. SR&ED investment tax credits (15% refundable/35% non-CCPC) and accelerated CCA (Class 12, 50%) for qualifying software/equipment; e-commerce sales fully taxable at general rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) approved software under the Corporation Internet Filing (CIF) / NETFILE service; Alberta provincial corporate tax is assessed through the integrated T2 provincial schedule (Schedule 5).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within 6 months after the taxation year-end; balance of tax due within 2 months after year-end for ULCs that are non-CCPCs (3 months for CCPC portion); quarterly installments due when net tax owing exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the fiscal year (gross revenue less deductions and loss carryovers).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: ULC is a Canadian resident corporation by incorporation; report worldwide income, no non-resident election available for the entity itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax at the 15% general rate on Lines 100 income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply federal tax credits (foreign tax credits, SR&ED) only if attributable to Canadian-source operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial tax at 8% computed on Alberta taxable income allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate revenue to Alberta using statutory apportionment; for a single-province operation, allocate 100% of taxable income to Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable net of installments and credits; transfers to federal/provincial accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, the withholding remittance is separate from the T2; do not net Part XIII withholding against T2 balance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return for non-arm's length transactions with non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when aggregate gross remuneration/value of transactions with related non-residents exceeds CAD 1,000,000; attach to T2 or file separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (max 12 months) for repeat failures; late payments accrue daily compounded prescribed-rate interest (currently ~8-9%); failure to file Schedule 8/T106 attracts an additional penalty of CAD 100 per day (min CAD 1,000) and potential gross negligence penalties under s. 163(2) of up to 50% of understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (recoverable by the payee as set-off against Canadian tax if the shareholder is a Canadian-resident corporation).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Canada-US DTA, US-resident corporate shareholders owning at least 10% of the ULC's voting stock qualify for a 5% withholding rate; other US residents qualify for 15%. Protocol: (1) obtain a US Certificate of Residency (IRS Form 6166 / TRC); (2) submit Form NR301 (Declaration of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits) to the paying corporation; (3) the paying corporation withholds at the treaty rate only if the NR301 and TRC are in hand before payment; (4) if the full 25% was withheld, recipient applies for refund via Form NR7-R with CRA; (5) re-file reduced withholding annually upon TRC expiry. LOB clause must be satisfied: the US shareholder must be a qualified person (listed company, active trade or business test, or derivative benefits).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% Part XIII; Canada-US treaty rate 10% (0% for copyright royalties), subject to TRC and NR301. Interest: statutory 25%; treaty rate 15% generally, and 0% for eligible arm's-length long-term interest; anti-avoidance rules may recharacterize excessive interest as a dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 gross transaction value per non-arm's length non-resident counterparty triggers mandatory T106 reporting and contemporaneous TP documentation (Local/Master File benchmark study must be prepared within 3 months after fiscal year-end to avoid s. 247(3) penalties).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies GAAR (s. 245 Income Tax Act) and treaty Limitation on Benefits clauses. A ULC retailing cosmetics online must demonstrate Canadian substance: physical inventory storage in Alberta, centralized management of returns/logistics, employee decision-making on pricing and suppliers, board meetings in Canada, and substantive e-commerce contracts. Mere flow-through of funds through a ULC without Alberta-based operational substance risks treaty denial on dividends and GAAR reclassification. No separate ESR filing exists in Canada, but substance documentation is required to defend the corporate residence and beneficial-ownership claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Shopify/PayPal gross sales, false COGS deductions, or undisclosed offshore merchant accounts; creating shell invoices for fake marketing services from a non-arm's length foreign entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA civil penalty under s. 163(2) of 50% of the tax evaded, plus interest and full reassessment; criminal prosecution under s. 239 ITA for tax evasion: fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; seizure and freeze of bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally assessed under s. 227.1 ITA for corporate withholding taxes and GST/HST if the ULC fails to remit; criminal fines can be imposed on the directing mind; travel bans and exit controls under CRA collections; civil restitution and director disqualification in Alberta.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance / Unremitted Part XIII
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or management fees to non-resident shareholders without withholding 25% or the treaty rate; failing to file NR4 returns and remit to CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Part XIII tax becomes immediately payable, plus late-planning penalties of 10% of the unremitted amount, daily compounding interest, and potential 50% gross negligence penalty if the omission is considered intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for the full unremitted Part XIII tax, interest, and penalties; CRA may issue a director liability assessment and enforce against personal assets; willful evasion may lead to criminal charges and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transactions with related US/offshore entities exceeding CAD 1,000,000 without a contemporaneous TP study; paying supra-competitive royalties to a related IP-holding company; under-reporting intercompany management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s. 247(3) applies a 10% penalty on the net transfer pricing adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000) if the taxpayer failed to make reasonable documentation efforts; unreported T106 filings attract CAD 100/day penalties; the underlying tax is re-assessed with interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors not automatically joint and severally liable for TP penalties under s. 247, but gross negligence or false statements are subject to s. 163(2)/(3) penalties and director criminal liability under s. 239; CRA may pursue negligent directors in cases of egregious foreign profit shifting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming the ULC solely to access the Canada-US treaty flow-through benefit without carrying on active beauty retail; routing sales through a ULC that has no inventory, employees, contracts, or management in Canada; using ULC to convert income into dividends with nil economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under s. 245 disallows the tax benefit and recharacterizes the distribution to the foreign parent; a further misrepresentation penalty of 25% of the benefit may apply where a transaction is attributed to a misrepresentation; the CRA can reassess within 3 to 10 years, disregarding the normal limitation period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a foreign parent that caused the ULC to be a sham may be treated as directing minds; Canadian courts can pierce the ULC's unlimited liability shield, impose restitution for tax avoided, issue travel bans against directors, and in criminal tax evasion cases impose imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the beauty retail business with high-volume Shopify/PayPal deposits, using the ULC account to launder proceeds from foreign undisclosed sources, structuring deposits to avoid reporting or failing the corporate AML program (risk assessment, compliance officer, training, and record keeping).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for entities; failure to report a suspicious transaction (STR) leads to penalties of up to CAD 2,000,000 per occurrence for third parties such as banks; criminal offence of laundering under Criminal Code s. 462.31 attracts up to 10 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who directed, authorized, or assented to AML breaches face personal fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months (summary) or 5 years (indictable) under PCMLTFA; asset forfeiture orders and travel bans apply to directors involved in cross-border laundering flows.
